- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots downward; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above true price, adjust downward by 1–2% per period.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment >0.7, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment unit above 0.5.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/1.00), model overfits short-term noise; apply a 3-period moving average filter to forecast.
